newsitem.title: UK: Berisford sets max loan stock price at 73p.
newsitem.headline: Berisford sets max loan stock price at 73p.

text.p: Catering equipment manufacturer Berisford Plc said on Tuesday that it had set the maximum price for purchasing some or all of its five percent convertible unsecured loan stock 2015 from at up to 73 pence per unit.
In a statement, the company said the maximum price represented a premium of 10 percent over the closing mid-market quotation of 66.5 pence on December 2, 1996.

The price also represents a premium of about 33 percent over the closing mid-market quotation of 54.75 pence on November 14, 1996, the day it announced intentions to purchase a proportion of the stock.

Decision on the buyback was stalled for a few days after Berisford said it had received an offer of interest from a suitor. The company's share price rose from around 130 to 150 pence. The suitor's name was not announced.
Berisford said on Monday that the suitor had withdrawn its interest.
The company said it would purchase up to 100 million units of the stock although it reserved the right to increase or decrease the tender size.
The tender invitation would close on Wednesday, December 11, 1996. The results would be announced the following day.
